sources.entry: pgcli - PostgreSQL CLI with autocompletion and syntax highlighting.

summary.one_liner: pgcli is a PostgreSQL command-line client (a REPL) with auto-completion and syntax highlighting.
summary.what_it_does: pgcli is an interactive Postgres client that suggests SQL keywords, tables and columns as you type. It highlights syntax using Pygments and is built on prompt_toolkit. Its smart completion is context-sensitive, so after FROM it shows only table names and after WHERE it shows only column names. It supports a primitive set of psql backslash commands and pretty-prints tabular results. It accepts connection details as a database name or a postgresql:// URL, and honors many PG* environment variables and SSL settings. A config file is created at ~/.config/pgcli/config on first launch.
use_cases: query a PostgreSQL database from the terminal
autocomplete SQL table and column names
connect to Postgres over SSL from the command line
run Postgres queries inside an IPython session
browse Postgres databases with a friendlier shell than psql
run pgcli from Docker without a system install
how_to_run: sudo apt-get install pgcli  # Debian-based Linux only
notable: Context-sensitive smart completion (table names after FROM, column names after WHERE)
Supports many psql environment variables such as PGHOST, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and SSL settings
IPython magic (%pgcli) that stores query results in the IPython workspace
--warn option to prompt before destructive queries
--auto-vertical-output and row-limit prompt for wide or large results
caveats: Only supports PostgreSQL; the README mentions a MySQL equivalent project but this one targets Postgres
psql backslash command support is described as primitive
Pip install needs Postgres installed on the system, per the README
